feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: iteration 5 (span plus or minus 0.036 m, 12 mm footprints, lead 0.06 m, wheel_track 0.10 m) scored 653.3, the best so far. Its oval finished 20/20 at 1.85 s, and its s-bend finished 18/20 with steering_oscillation 0.335. Its slalom was 0/20 with 1.0 line-loss events and max_error 0.0644. Iteration 6 (lead 0.07 m) left the slalom at 0/20 with 1.0 events and max_error 0.065, and its s-bend steering_oscillation was 0.333. Lead and reach are therefore not the limit, which points to yaw response. Lowering yaw inertia by about 40 percent should help the robot change heading at the slalom's direction changes. The main side effect to watch is s-bend jitter, since the s-bend oscillation has been near the 0.35 limit in every run since iteration 1. Next-race rules: if slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 or max_error drops below 0.06, keep the inertia change and report slalom completion_time if any trial finishes. If slalom line loss is unchanged at about 1.0 with max_error at or above 0.06, the yaw response is not the limit, so report the heading at first line loss so the next step can target controller entry speed. If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above 0.35, return to mass 0.7 kg and body_length 0.16 m.
requested_changes: If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 (iterations 5 and 6 measured 0.335 and 0.333 at the current inertia), return mass to 0.7 kg and body_length to 0.16 m, keeping the iteration 5 span, lead and drivetrain.

If slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 but no trial finishes (iteration 5 max_error 0.0644 with 1.0 events), try mass 0.5 kg with body_length 0.12 m to reduce yaw inertia further, while keeping steering_oscillation under 0.35 on the s-bend.

If the oval loses any trials or the slalom line loss stays at about 1.0 with max_error at or above 0.06, try wheel_track 0.09 m for more turn authority. Iteration 4 showed the oval at 20/20 with wheel_track 0.10 m (1.82 s), so the time margin is there.
